round 6 follow-up, Fabio's screenshot: the review track was a flat fill. A take under review is not a file, so ffmpeg extractAudioWaveform cannot run and there is no mask to hand MpiWaveform. bakeWaveMask() now draws showwavespic shape in the renderer - mono, sqrt, white-on-transparent, same 1260x540 - applied after the player mounts and only if that instance is still the mounted one.

mask pixels measured: silence 0.002 of column height, loud 0.952, -30 dBFS 0.174 (linear would draw ~0.03 - that is what sqrt buys). Committed check: gallery-audio-waveform.spec.js "a take under review bakes its own waveform mask", passes 9.6s. npm test 1418/1419, 0 fail. Lint clean.

two from Fabio accepting a take: (1) PRE-EXISTING, folded in - mediaImportService._buildGroup dropped thumbPath on the AUDIO branch only, so every fresh audio card was blank until the project was reopened and the sidecar read back; (2) bakeWaveMask column is RMS now, not the bucket peak.

measured both bakes on voices/child_1.opus (mean ink / jaggedness): ffmpeg 0.173/0.021, ours by peak 0.289/0.037, ours by RMS 0.193/0.023 - the peak of 340 samples made neighbours disagree, which aliased into the smear Fabio called blurry. Spec threshold moved 0.8 -> 0.7 because a sine RMS is 1/sqrt(2) of peak, with the arithmetic stated. thumbPath test proven RED on un-fixed source. npm test 1419/1420, desktop spec green, lint clean.

round 7, the gallery card kind chip. Fabio picked it over the card mark and widened it: colour the icon AND badge image + audio, so every kind states its media type. ASSET_KINDS gained an `accent` column holding a [data-accent] value; MpiGalleryGrid writes it onto the chip, which rebinds --accent-heat for itself, and the chip color came off --ink-1. No new token, no color-mix between two family accents. image->vision, video->video, audio->audio, gif->video, scene->vision (last two flagged as judgement calls before building, not corrected).

npm test 1429/1430 (1 skipped, 0 fail), gallery-filter-panel.spec.js green on its own port, eslint --max-warnings=0 clean on all four touched JS files. New spec step asserts the chip data-accent per card AND that img1.color !== vid1.color in real Electron - that is what fails if the attribute is dropped or misspelt, because a bad value matches nothing and the chip silently inherits #app-shell. Edge that badge:true on `image` created: kindOfItem catch-all matches undefined, so an empty card would have claimed to be an image; guarded at the one call site, not in kindOfItem (six callers, one not optional-chained). First suite run failed twice in gif-frames.test.cjs on mkdtemp ENOENT for a missing %TEMP%/cubric-tests parent - environmental, 10/10 green alone, 161 GB free, file untouched. round 7, two corrections from Fabio on the first app pass. (1) GIF moves off `video` onto `vision`: "I know they're animated, but they're still images" - the accent splits by what the thing IS, not by whether it moves, which also settles 3D Scene staying rose until the app does real 3D MODELS (his words: that is when it earns its own hue and mascot). (2) "another place we're forgetting colour is the filters" - the filter panel kind rows now carry [data-accent] too, so an active row fills with the family colour instead of the workspace accent and cannot disagree with the card chip. Mark rows and the previews flag pass none: not media types.

filter panel needed NO css value change - .mpi-gallery-filter__row:has(.is-active) already filled with var(--accent-heat), so setting [data-accent] on the row was the whole fix. The <body>-portal trap (structural cause #5) does not bite: the row declares its own --accent-heat rather than inheriting one. Dark ink on the fill (oklch(0.20 0.03 355)) needs no per-hue variant - every family accent is L 0.76-0.88.
